tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: The page ground. Every screen, panel and popover sits on this; it is the default ground for `ink`, `ink-muted` and `ink-faint`.

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Wells that recede: input fields, the raw-JSON pane, an empty screen before the first run.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Panels, report cards, the sticky screen header and popovers. Second ground for `ink`, `ink-muted` and `ink-faint`.

tokens.name: surface-hover
tokens.usage: Screen-row and menu-item hover. A transient state only — never paint a resting element with it.

tokens.name: surface-selected
tokens.usage: The selected screen row and the active tab, always together with a 2px `accent` left edge so selection is not colour alone.

tokens.name: hairline
tokens.usage: The 1px rules between screen rows and inside panels. Decorative structure only: it never carries meaning on its own, which is why it sits below the 3:1 floor.

tokens.name: border
tokens.usage: Borders on anything that carries meaning: inputs, buttons, chips, the band track, the validity bar. Holds 3:1 on `surface`, `surface-raised` and `surface-sunken` in both themes.

tokens.name: border-strong
tokens.usage: Hovered or active control borders, and the two endpoints of the fair band in `BandMeter`.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and every figure, on `surface`, `surface-raised`, `surface-sunken` and `surface-selected`.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Column headers, field labels and secondary prose on `surface` and `surface-raised`.

tokens.name: ink-faint
tokens.usage: Dates, units, placeholders and disabled text on `surface` and `surface-raised`. Still above 4.5:1 in both themes — nothing in Fairband is deliberately hard to read.

tokens.name: ink-inverse
tokens.usage: Text on an `ink` or `border-strong` fill, such as the price marker's callout in `BandMeter`.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: The one accent: links, focus, the selected row's edge, the Fairband wordmark, and a price below the band. Reads above 4.5:1 as text on `surface` and `surface-raised` in both themes.

tokens.name: accent-hover
tokens.usage: Hover and active state for anything painted `accent`.

tokens.name: accent-quiet
tokens.usage: Tinted ground behind accent chips, the fair segment of the band track and the selected row. Put `ink` or `accent` on it, never `ink-faint`.

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text and glyphs on an `accent` fill, such as the primary button.

tokens.name: caution
tokens.usage: Attention, not failure: a value past two thirds of its validity window, and a price above the fair band. Reads above 4.5:1 as text on `surface` and `surface-raised`.

tokens.name: caution-quiet
tokens.usage: Ground behind aging-value chips and the above-band region of `BandMeter`.

tokens.name: on-caution
tokens.usage: Text and glyphs on a `caution` fill.

tokens.name: critical
tokens.usage: A value past its validity window, a rejected report, a destructive action. Reads above 4.5:1 as text on `surface` and `surface-raised`.

tokens.name: critical-quiet
tokens.usage: Ground behind expired-value marks and rejected-report headers.

tokens.name: on-critical
tokens.usage: Text and glyphs on a `critical` fill.

tokens.name: prov-derived
tokens.usage: The ƒ glyph, which marks a number the engine computed. Deliberately neutral: the basis word beside it — mechanical or reviewed — is the signal, not the colour.

tokens.name: prov-input
tokens.usage: The ◆ glyph, which marks a write rather than a computed number. Reads above 4.5:1 on `surface`, `surface-raised` and `prov-input-quiet`. It never implies who wrote — the principal beside it says that.

tokens.name: prov-input-quiet
tokens.usage: Ground behind a principal chip that needs weight, and the header of a pending `ReportCard`. Carries `prov-input` and `ink`.

tokens.name: phase-1
tokens.usage: Life-cycle phase 1, Start-up. The lightest step of the ramp; the phase number beside it is the primary signal.

tokens.name: phase-2
tokens.usage: Life-cycle phase 2, Young growth.

tokens.name: phase-3
tokens.usage: Life-cycle phase 3, High growth.

tokens.name: phase-4
tokens.usage: Life-cycle phase 4, Mature growth.

tokens.name: phase-5
tokens.usage: Life-cycle phase 5, Mature stable.

tokens.name: phase-6
tokens.usage: Life-cycle phase 6, Decline. The darkest step; the ramp runs cool to warm and light to dark so the six phases order themselves by lightness as well as hue.

tokens.name: focus-ring
tokens.usage: The 2px focus ring, offset 2px, on every focusable control. Solid, never dashed, and above 3:1 on `surface`, `surface-raised` and `surface-sunken`.

tokens.name: chart-1
tokens.usage: The one series hue, for lines, bars and dots. Fairband charts use emphasis, not categorical colour: one subject in this hue, everything else in `chart-context`. Clears 3:1 as a mark on `surface` and `surface-raised` in both themes.

tokens.name: chart-context
tokens.usage: The de-emphasis grey: the hurdle line in `SpreadChart`, context series, and any mark that is reference rather than subject. Holds 3:1 on `surface` as a meaningful mark.

tokens.name: chart-grid
tokens.usage: Gridlines and axis rules, one step off the surface, 1px and always solid. Chrome, not data, so it is exempt from the 3:1 floor — like `hairline`.

tokens.name: chart-band
tokens.usage: The fair-value band as a wash behind the price line in `BandHistory` — the series hue at roughly 10%, never a saturated block. Its edges are drawn in `border-strong`, matching `BandMeter`.

tokens.name: chart-mid
tokens.usage: The neutral midpoint of the diverging scale: a cell or segment sitting at the baseline. It must read as nothing, so it carries no hue — but it is a step off the surface rather than a well, so a midpoint cell reads as present and neutral, not as missing data.

tokens.name: chart-pos-1
tokens.usage: Diverging positive arm, step 1 of 3 — value above the baseline by the least. Carries `ink` as an in-cell label. Validated: monotone lightness, step gaps above 0.06, light end above 2:1 on `surface`.

tokens.name: chart-pos-2
tokens.usage: Diverging positive arm, step 2 of 3. Carries `ink` as an in-cell label at 4.7:1 or better in both themes.

tokens.name: chart-pos-3
tokens.usage: Diverging positive arm, step 3 of 3 — the strongest step, and the same value as `zone-buy`, so a positive bar and the buy zone can never disagree. This step inverts: it carries `ink-inverse` as an in-cell label, not `ink`.

tokens.name: chart-neg-1
tokens.usage: Diverging negative arm, step 1 of 3 — value below the baseline by the least. Carries `ink` as an in-cell label. Terracotta against the cool positive arm: warm versus cool, so the poles read as opposite without ever being a red/green pair.

tokens.name: chart-neg-2
tokens.usage: Diverging negative arm, step 2 of 3. Carries `ink` as an in-cell label.

tokens.name: chart-neg-3
tokens.usage: Diverging negative arm, step 3 of 3 — the strongest step, and the same value as `zone-trim`. Carries `ink-inverse` as an in-cell label, not `ink`.

tokens.name: zone-buy
tokens.usage: The region of the value axis below the buy level, in `BandMeter`. A green-leaning teal: it reads as green while staying off the red/green axis, which fails for roughly one man in twelve. Carries `ink-inverse` for its zone word.

tokens.name: zone-hold
tokens.usage: The region between the buy and trim levels. Deliberately colourless — hold means nothing to do — and told apart from `zone-fair` by lightness rather than hue. Carries `ink-faint` for its zone word.

tokens.name: zone-fair
tokens.usage: The fair band itself, drawn as a raised region inside `zone-hold`. Still no hue: fair is neither cheap nor dear, and a yellow here would say caution, which is what `caution` already means.

tokens.name: zone-trim
tokens.usage: The region at and above the trim level. A terracotta that reads as red without being `critical`, which stays reserved for expired and rejected. Carries `ink-inverse` for its zone word.

tokens.name: stance-buy
tokens.usage: The word "Buy" — price below the buy level. Always the word, never the colour alone; the zone it names wears the same value.

tokens.name: stance-hold
tokens.usage: The word "Hold" — price between the buy and trim levels. Colourless on purpose.

tokens.name: stance-trim
tokens.usage: The word "Trim" — price at or above the trim level. Always the word, never the colour alone.

tokens.name: record-applied
tokens.usage: A record that went through: an override applied, a report published, a proposal confirmed. The record is done and nothing is being asked of the reader.

tokens.name: record-pending
tokens.usage: A proposal waiting for the Owner — the only state in which a record asks the reader for something. No other agent record is ever pending.

tokens.name: record-refused
tokens.usage: A refused override, a rejected report, a rejected proposal. The attempt is over: resubmitting it unchanged will fail the same way.

tokens.name: record-stale
tokens.usage: A stale-revision conflict or a stale proposal. Deliberately not `record-refused`: nothing is wrong with the write, it was aimed at a revision that has moved, and it succeeds once rebased.

styles.name: display
styles.usage: The page title, and a company's name at the top of its detail view. One per page.

styles.name: title
styles.usage: Panel titles: Screen, Inputs, Band, Reports.

styles.name: heading
styles.usage: Subsection headings inside a panel, and headings in these guidelines.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Reason: 10-K shows a third plant coming online in FY27.
styles.usage: Prose: guidelines, report summaries, and the reason attached to every input change.

styles.name: control
styles.usage: Text inside an interactive control — buttons, inputs, menu items, tabs. The only style that lives inside a control.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Field labels and screen column headers. Set in uppercase in the UI; the tracking exists for that.

styles.name: caption
styles.usage: The three dates, units, provenance meta and row counts. Never the only place a number appears.

styles.name: figure
styles.usage: Every number in a table cell. Monospaced so a column of figures aligns on the decimal with no extra work.

styles.name: figure-lg
styles.usage: The headline price and value per share on a company's detail view.

styles.name: figure-sm
styles.usage: Band endpoints, deltas, from/to pairs in a report, and input tags.

styles.name: ticker
styles.usage: Ticker symbols in the screen's first column and in page titles.

spacing.note: A 4px grid. The screen is dense, so steps 1 through 3 do most of the work.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Gap between a provenance glyph and its figure; inset of a dense table cell.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Vertical padding in a screen row; gap between chips in a row.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Horizontal padding in a screen cell; gap between form rows.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Panel padding, card padding, and the gap between panels.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Gap between a panel's title and its first row.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Spacing between sections inside a panel; the cover's rule pitch divides by this.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Gap between major regions: screen, detail, reports.

tokens.name: space-10
tokens.usage: Page gutter, left and right.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: Space above a page title.

radius.note: Small and consistent. Fairband is an instrument, not a card wall.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Chips, phase badges, the band track, and the cover's colour blocks.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs, select menus.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: Panels, report cards, popovers.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Only two things: the provenance dot and the price marker's cap.

shadow.note: Fairband separates with `hairline` and `border`. Shadow is reserved for things that float above the page.

tokens.name: shadow-popover
tokens.usage: Popovers, the reason tooltip and the column menu. The only shadow in the app.

tokens.name: shadow-well
tokens.usage: The top edge of a `surface-sunken` well, so an input reads as recessed without a heavier border.

size.note: Fixed measures the screen depends on. Change these and row rhythm changes everywhere.

tokens.name: header-height
tokens.usage: The application header. Short on purpose — it is chrome, and every pixel above the screen is a row the reader does not get.

tokens.name: row-height
tokens.usage: A screen row at default density.

tokens.name: row-height-dense
tokens.usage: A screen row with `dense` set, for fitting the whole universe on one page.

tokens.name: figure-column
tokens.usage: Minimum width of a numeric column, so a figure never wraps.

tokens.name: detail-rail
tokens.usage: Width of the inputs rail beside a company's detail view.

tokens.name: band-track
tokens.usage: Height of the `ValidityWindow` track — a thin bar with no regions to label.

tokens.name: zone-track
tokens.usage: Height of the `BandMeter` track. Taller than `band-track` because its three zones carry their words inside them.

tokens.name: chart-height
tokens.usage: Plot height for a chart in a company report, excluding its axis band. `BandHistory` is the one chart that takes more.

tokens.name: chart-bar-max
tokens.usage: Maximum bar thickness in `HistoryBars`. A bar never fills its slot — the leftover is air.
